subject: MRDS in Distance 7 - error message 'object field'

messages.author: ff49ef0865299d94
messages.subject: MRDS in Distance 7 - error message 'object field'
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am using Distance 7 to analyze a line transect aerial survey with a double observer platform. When selecting MRDS I receive the following error message:

** Error: Some values in the object field are not unique **

However, all object fields have unique numbers, except that the same number appears twice, for observer 1 and observer 2 as required in a double observer platform (mark-recapture) setup. Below/attached is a screenshot of the data setup in Distance. I fail to understand why the MRDS engine does not read the file as a double observer platform with unique object fields and why the error message comes up.


Thank you in advance for any suggestions!


Kerstin

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS in Distance 7 - error message 'object field'
parts:
Kerstin

I agree the screenshot you show appears to have everything organised properly.  There are two things you might double check

- Dave Miller suggested that you be sure you selected "double observer" with the project wizard when you created the project.  You can double check by examining properties of the survey: survey tab, open "New Survey", check configuration (as shown below)

- The other check is that *all* of your detected objects have 2 records associated with them; it is easy to overlook one object somewhere in your data.

messages.author: ff49ef0865299d94
messages.subject: Re: MRDS in Distance 7 - error message 'object field'
parts:
Hi Eric,

Thank you and Dave Miller very much for your suggestions. I double checked my project and I had correctly selected "double observer" with the project wizard when I created the project. I also double checked all the object fields and all of the detected objects had two records.

However, your suggestion pointed me in the right direction and I started reducing the data set down to smaller sub-sections to create smaller input files to see which part of the data worked and which caused the error. I then finally realized that one of the detected objects with two records had different transect numbers assigned! Once I corrected the transect number, the error message disappeared and the analyses ran.

Thank you so much for your help, it was as you mentioned a typo in the input file!

Kerstin
